answer: Cap new identities to a fixed quota per epoch, sold by a descending-price Dutch auction. A lone joiner waits for the price to ripple down and grabs a cheap tail seat; but an operator wanting a thousand clones must sweep the whole scarce batch at once, bidding the price back up against itself. Flooding costs climb like scaling frozen tundra, not sliding down a shale slope. A hard seat-cap means no swarm can mint faster than the auction releases, so fakes stay rare and dear.
